title: performance: perf-canary auto-detect + hysteresis rollout guards
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Motivation: improve our performance canary subsystem to automatically detect latency and throughput regressions, and to prevent unsafe automated rollouts when transient noise or KV-cache churn causes spikes. This PR introduces a new detector that computes rolling baselines, applies hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping, and wires rollout guards into the canary controller.

What this changes: - New autodetect detector implementation (perf/canary/detector.go) that computes p50/p95 latency baselines and throughput baselines per-model and per-route. - Hysteresis and grace windows configurable per-customer and per-environment to avoid unstable rollouts. - Integration with rollout policy engine: canary controller will now pause `auto-shift` if detector reports regression or high variance. - Added observability: new metrics (perf_canary.detector_regressions, perf_canary.hysteresis_state), dashboards, and alerts. - End-to-end tests and unit tests for detector logic and hysteresis. - Docs: perf-canary.md updated with configuration and tuning guidance.

Checklist: - [x] Detector implementation + unit tests - [x] Canary controller integration + end-to-end test - [x] Dashboard panels + alert rules - [x] Feature flag gating (feature_perf_canary_autodetect) - [x] Backwards compatible config - [x] Release notes

Compatibility & rollout: The feature is behind a feature flag and disabled for existing default stacks. We will enable progressively for internal staging and a limited subset of customers. The detector is conservative by default (wide thresholds + long grace window) to minimize false positives.

Related: ENG-9382 (perf canary improvements), ENG-9420 (rollout safety), SUP-2021 (customer-reported canary flapping). References: #51731 (previous hysteresis prototype), internal RFC: rfc/perf-canary-autodetect.md.

Notes: I focused on correctness and observability over aggressive thresholds. Ops can tune thresholds from the console and we have default recommendations in docs.
